value.hook: Read before accepting $UID/$EUID as a trusted identity in a just recipe or shell script.
value.title: macOS bash 3.2 imports UID and EUID from the environment

sections.name: body
sections.value: #299 F247 swapped $(id -u) for bash's $UID. On macOS, #!/usr/bin/env bash usually resolves to /bin/bash 3.2.57, which takes UID and EUID from the environment (env UID=0 bash -c 'echo $UID' prints 0; bash 5 refuses, readonly). Numeric spoofs fail closed in bounce-rs (lsof -u <other> exits 1 for non-root), but lsof grammar does not: -u '^501' exits 0 with empty output, which skips the holder check silently. Graded a C33 operator-env note (S299-N2), not a block, since PIJ_BOUNCE_LSOF already grants the same. Fix shape: a digits-only case guard before use. Also #299: the Linux sweep's foreign skip is bounded by ours() file-owner checks, so only root-held or uid-dropped fds can escape it.
